summary: Map navigation prior v1 failed its predeclared frozen-policy gate. Across 72 paired unseen-seed episodes, mean progress rose only from 1.0556 to 1.0694, progress improved in one of three policy modes, step-limit rate fell from 23.61% to 15.28% rather than halving, and neither arm produced a staircase exit or Zone 2 entry. The prior was disabled by any visible enemy, activating on only 0.87% of deterministic turns and leaving long valid-movement cycles intact. One stochastic sample improved accidental Floor 2 descents, which is insufficient evidence of navigational competence. Raw item-pickup retention is non-authoritative because seed 62023 repeatedly swapped items and inflated pickups to 2,485 while adding only one unique item type. Retain current-11; the next navigation design must use local-threat gating, frontier planning, remembered hazards, staircase exits as the causal progress measure, and corrected lexicographic level tracking.
